$comment: The scope registry. This file must live where the repositories it governs cannot write to it —
a separate, restricted repository, alongside the trusted enforcement workflow. StandardsEnforcer
refuses a registry located inside the repository being assessed.
Entries are keyed by immutable platform identity, never by name. `acme/moneyball` can be renamed,
transferred, deleted and recreated by somebody else; a decision that follows a name follows
whoever holds the name today. `name` is present for humans and is never matched on.
Dispositions are filed under `standards`, keyed by the asking pack's own contract id, because the
unit of applicability is repository x standards pack. A repository may be in scope for one standard
and out of scope for another, each with its own reviewer, date, reason and basis. Silence about a
pack is a question, not an answer: no decision on file is review-required, and never inherits
`reviewedFootprint` is the evidence basis, and it NAMES THE SURFACE it was reviewed against. It is
what makes a decision able to go stale, and a decision that cannot go stale cannot be trusted to be
fresh. Obtain it with `node scripts/footprint.mjs <dir>`. A basis naming a surface the enforcer did
not observe on a run is undetermined — neither fresh nor stale — and goes back to a human. There is
one detector today; a pack with no detector is not a pack whose detector found nothing.
An out-of-scope entry needs exactly the same quality of record as an in-scope one. An exclusion
is a governance decision, not an absence of evidence.
